blocks.text: These two Names are found in authentic ahaadeeth from the Prophet ﷺ. An example of which is that Abu Musa narrated that the Prophet ﷺ used to invoke Allaah with the following invocation:

"O Lord forgive me my faults, my ignorance, my immoderation in all my affairs. You are more knowing about them than myself. O Allaah, grant me forgiveness for my faults the ones that I committed deliberately, unintentionally or out of jest and all that I did. O Allaah, grant me forgiveness for what I put forward or sent back, what I committed secretly or in the open. You are the One who gives precedence and the One who puts back and You are able to do all things." Agreed upon (found in Saheeh Al-Bukhaaree and Saheeh Muslim)

These two Names are from those that are paired opposites. One Name cannot be used alone for Allaah without the other as perfection comes when the two Names are together. Giving precedence and putting back are two descriptions of Allaah indicating Allaah's perfect Ability, execution of His Will and His complete Wisdom.

They are from His Attributes of Action as giving precedence and putting back are connected to the creation in self, action and description. This giving precedence and putting back is universal such as the giving precedence to some of creation over others or putting back some of creation over others. It is also like giving precedence to the cause and overall effect; and the conditions over their agreements among other examples. Another example of giving precedence and putting back is in creation and predestination.

Examples of giving precedence and putting back in terms of legislation is where the Prophets are better than the creation. Some Prophets are better than others. Some of his servants are better than others. He gave precedence to them in knowledge, faith, action, manners and in all descriptions and He also put them back with some of those. All of this is according to His wisdom. He puts forward whoever He wills of His creation to His mercy by His success and grace and He puts back whoever He wills of that by His justice.

These two names occur in the context of seeking forgiveness for all sins put forward and put back, secret and open, mistakenly done or intended. From this it is known that sins put back a servant and destroys him. Allaah forgiving and pardoning His servant gives him precedence and raises him. Command is all for Allaah in His hand. He debases and raises, He gives honour and humiliates, He gives and prevents whomever Allaah has written to have honour, status and precedence and no one can prevent him from that. Whoever Allaah has written to be humiliated, debased and put back, no one can help him escape from that.

From the fruits of believing in this Name is having motivation to give precedence to what Allaah gave precedence to and to put back what Allaah put back. The Prophet ﷺ had strong motivation in seeking to give precedence to what Allaah gave precedence to and to start with what He started with. Due to this he started with (Mount) Safaa in the Sa'ee. He ﷺ said, 'We begin with what Allaah began with'. He ﷺ started with the face, the two hands and then the head in ritual ablution (wudhoo). He did not change this even once.

This is so in all the affairs of the religion. It is obligatory to give precedence to whoever Allaah gave precedence to and to put back those that He put back. Also to love those He loved and hate those He hated. This is the most trustworthy handhold of faith.

keyPoints: Al-Muqaddim and Al-Mu'akhkhir are found in authentic ahaadeeth, such as the Prophet's ﷺ invocation: "You are the One who gives precedence and the One who puts back."
They are paired opposite Names: one cannot be used alone for Allaah without the other, as perfection comes when the two are together.
Giving precedence and putting back indicate Allaah's perfect Ability, execution of His Will and His complete Wisdom, and are from His Attributes of Action.
Giving precedence and putting back is both universal (in creation and predestination) and legislative (e.g. the Prophets being better than the creation and some Prophets better than others).
Sins put back a servant and destroy him, while Allaah's forgiveness and pardon give him precedence and raise him.
A fruit of believing in these Names is giving precedence to what Allaah gave precedence to and putting back what He put back, as the Prophet ﷺ began with Safaa and followed the order of wudhoo.

evidence.text: "...O Allaah, grant me forgiveness for what I put forward or sent back, what I committed secretly or in the open. You are the One who gives precedence and the One who puts back and You are able to do all things."

recall.q: Why can't one of these two Names be used alone for Allaah?
recall.a: Because they are paired opposites, and perfection comes when the two Names are together.

recall.q: In which hadeeth do these two Names occur?
recall.a: In the Prophet's ﷺ invocation for forgiveness narrated by Abu Musa: "...You are the One who gives precedence and the One who puts back and You are able to do all things" (Agreed upon).

recall.q: Give an example from the chapter of the Prophet ﷺ giving precedence to what Allaah gave precedence to.
recall.a: He started with Safaa in the Sa'ee, saying 'We begin with what Allaah began with', and he started with the face, the two hands and then the head in wudhoo, never changing this.
